hook: In German, „Das ist ja großartig“ can mean disaster: learn to hear irony in a flat voice, and when to choose understatement instead.
intro: Twelve sentences that live on tone, to listen to and repeat: ironic praise (Na, das ist ja großartig gelaufen; Das hast du ja wieder mal toll hinbekommen; Na toll, jetzt regnet es auch noch), the loaded particles ja, wohl and aber (Du bist ja ein Held; Das war wohl nichts; Du bist aber früh dran — said to someone who is late), mock formality (Wie überaus freundlich von Ihnen, uns das jetzt mitzuteilen), understatement (Nicht ganz optimal, würde ich sagen), the rhetorical wish (Schön wär's), deadpan (Ich bin begeistert) and two idioms of resignation (Da haben wir den Salat; Das kann ja heiter werden). Irony in German is carried by particles and by a flat, slightly slowed intonation — the words say one thing and the delivery says the opposite. Native speakers expect you to recognise it: an ironic großartig is a negative evaluation, and a speaker's real attitude often turns on exactly that. In a serious discussion with people you don't know well, do not use irony — it is easily misread and can sound dismissive towards your partner; understatement (nicht ganz optimal, nicht ganz überzeugend) is the safe way to be critical. Repeat each sentence twice: once straight, once ironic, and hear what changes.
tips[0].title: Particles that flip the meaning
tips[0].text: ja (Das ist ja großartig — with a flat tone: it isn't) · wohl (Das war wohl nichts — that was a failure) · aber (Du bist aber früh dran — said to a latecomer) · schön (Schön wär's — I wish). The particle plus the wrong tone equals irony.
tips[0].check.why: aber plus a flat tone flips the meaning: ‘early’ said to a latecomer means the opposite.
tips[0].visual.rows[2].a: Du bist mir ja ein schöner Freund.
tips[1].title: Understatement and mock formality
tips[1].text: Nicht ganz optimal (a disaster) · Wie überaus freundlich von Ihnen (how very kind — not) · Ich bin begeistert (deadpan). Politeness at the wrong temperature is irony. Understatement is the one form of it that is safe in a formal discussion.
tips[1].check.why: Understatement is critical but polite; ironic praise or deadpan enthusiasm can easily sound dismissive.
tips[2].title: Recognise it, don't aim it
tips[2].text: Irony is delivered without a smile in the voice: level pitch, slightly stretched vowels, a pause before the punchline. When you hear it, a positive word in that tone is a negative evaluation. When you speak with people you don't know well, leave irony out; use understatement if you must criticise.
tips[2].check.why: A positive word (toll) with ja and a flat, pausing delivery is a negative evaluation.
remember[0]: ja / wohl / aber / schön + flat tone = the opposite.
remember[1]: Recognise irony when listening; in a serious discussion prefer understatement.
exam: Recognising a speaker's attitude, irony included, is part of listening in the C1 exam; in its discussion, understatement is safer than irony.
tips[0].check.q: Said flatly to a friend who arrives forty minutes late: „Du bist aber früh dran.“ What does it mean?
tips[0].check.options[2]: You should come earlier next time.
tips[2].check.q: Someone says in a level voice, after a pause: „Das wird ja ein toller Abend.“ What do they mean?
tips[2].check.options[0]: They expect the evening to go badly.
tips[2].check.options[1]: They are looking forward to the evening.
tips[2].check.options[2]: They are asking whether the evening will be good.
tips[2].check.answer: They expect the evening to go badly.
